meta.blurb_uz: Shisha devorli shaharda yashovchi D-503 Yagona Davlatning fazoviy kemasini quradi. U o'z jamiyatini madh etish uchun kundalik yozishni boshlaydi, ammo tanishuvlar va kutilmagan voqealar uning ishonchini sinaydi.
meta.why_uz: Kundalik shaklidagi roman ingliz tilida shaxsiy hikoya, siyosiy til va matematik tashbehlar qanday yonma-yon kelishini ko'rsatadi.
meta.author_uz: Yevgeniy Zamyatin (1884–1937) — rus yozuvchisi va muhandisi. «Biz» romani ilk bor 1924-yilda Gregory Zilboorgning inglizcha tarjimasida nashr etilgan.
meta.edition_uz: To'liq matn. Inglizcha matn Gregory Zilboorgning 1924-yilgi tarjimasi (Standard Ebooks nashri); 40 qaydning hammasi berilgan. O'zbekcha parallel tarjima — WordDrop tarjimasi: har bir xatboshi inglizcha matndan qo'lda, asliga yaqin tarzda tarjima qilingan.

chapters.title: An announcement — The wisest of lines — A poem

paras.en: This is merely a copy, word by word, of what was published this morning in the State newspaper:
paras.uz: Quyidagilar bugun ertalab Davlat gazetasida chiqqan e'lonning so'zma-so'z nusxasi, xolos.

paras.en: “In another hundred and twenty days the building of the Integral will be completed. The great historic hour is near, when the first Integral will rise into the limitless space of the universe. A thousand years ago your heroic ancestors subjected the whole earth to the power of the United State. A still more glorious task is before you⁠—the integration of the indefinite equation of the Cosmos by the use of the glass, electric, fire-breathing Integral. Your mission is to subjugate to the grateful yoke of reason the unknown beings who live on other planets, and who are perhaps still in the primitive state of freedom. If they will not understand that we are bringing them a mathematically faultless happiness, our duty will be to force them to be happy. But before we take up arms, we shall try the power of words.
paras.uz: «Yana bir yuz yigirma kundan so'ng Integral qurilishi tugallanadi. Ulug' tarixiy soat yaqin: ilk Integral koinotning cheksiz fazosiga ko'tariladi. Ming yil avval qahramon ajdodlaringiz butun Yer yuzini Yagona Davlat hukmiga bo'ysundirdilar. Sizni bundan ham sharafliroq vazifa kutmoqda. Shishadan yasalgan, elektr quvvati bilan ishlaydigan, olov purkaydigan Integral vositasida koinotning noaniq tenglamasini integrallash kerak. Boshqa sayyoralarda yashovchi noma'lum mavjudotlar, ehtimol, hanuz ibtidoiy erkinlik holatidadir. Siz ularni aqlning minnatdorlikka arzigulik bo'yinturug'iga bo'ysundirishingiz kerak. Agar ular o'zlariga matematik jihatdan benuqson baxt olib borayotganimizni tushunmasalar, ularni baxtli bo'lishga majbur etish bizning burchimizdir. Ammo qurolga qo'l urishdan oldin so'zning kuchini sinab ko'ramiz.

paras.en: “In the name of The Well-Doer, the following is announced herewith to all Numbers of the United State:
paras.uz: «Homiyning nomidan Yagona Davlatning barcha Raqamlariga quyidagilar e'lon qilinadi.

paras.en: “Whoever feels capable must consider it his duty to write treatises, poems, manifestos, odes and other compositions on the greatness and the beauty of the United State.
paras.uz: «O'zida qobiliyat sezgan har kim Yagona Davlatning ulug'vorligi va go'zalligi haqida risola, she'r, manifest, qasida yoki boshqa asarlar yozishni o'z burchi deb bilsin.

paras.en: “This will be the first load which the Integral will carry.
paras.uz: «Bular Integral olib ketadigan ilk yuk bo'ladi.

paras.en: “Long live the United State! Long live the Numbers!! Long live the Well-Doer!!!”
paras.uz: «Yashasin Yagona Davlat! Yashasin Raqamlar!! Yashasin Homiy!!!»

paras.en: I feel my cheeks are burning as I write this. To integrate the colossal, universal equation! To unbend the wild curve, to straighten it out to a tangent⁠—to a straight line! For the United State is a straight line, a great, divine, precise, wise line, the wisest of lines!
paras.uz: Bularni yozar ekanman, yonoqlarim yonayotganini sezaman. Butun koinotning ulkan tenglamasini integrallash! O'zboshimcha egri chiziqni yoyib, urinmagacha — to'g'ri chiziqqacha rostlash! Negaki Yagona Davlat — to'g'ri chiziq. Ulug', ilohiy, aniq, dono chiziq, chiziqlarning eng donosi!

paras.en: I, D-503, the builder of the Integral, I am only one of the many mathematicians of the United State. My pen, which is accustomed to figures, is unable to express the march and rhythm of consonance; therefore I shall try to record only the things I see, the things I think, or to be more exact, the things we think. Yes, we; that is exactly what I mean, and “We” shall, therefore, be the title of my records. But this will only be a derivative of our life⁠—of our mathematical, perfect life in the United State. If this be so, will not this derivative be a poem in itself, despite my limitations? It will. I believe, I know it.
paras.uz: Men, D-503, Integral bunyodkori, Yagona Davlatdagi ko'p matematiklardan biriman, xolos. Raqamlarga o'rgangan qalamim ohangdoshlikning yurishi va ritmini ifodalay olmaydi. Shu bois ko'rganlarimni, o'ylaganlarimni, aniqrog'i, biz o'ylagan narsalarni yozib borishga urinaman. Ha, biz. Aytmoqchi bo'lganim aynan shu. Shuning uchun qaydlarimning nomi «Biz» bo'ladi. Ammo bu hayotimizning — Yagona Davlatdagi matematik, mukammal hayotimizning — hosilasigina bo'ladi. Shunday ekan, qobiliyatim cheklangan bo'lsa ham, shu hosilaning o'zi bir doston bo'lib chiqmaydimi? Chiqadi. Ishonaman, bilaman.

paras.en: I feel my cheeks are burning as I write this. I feel something similar to what a woman probably feels when for the first time she senses within herself the pulse of a tiny, blind, human being. It is I, and at the same time it is not I. And for many long months it will be necessary to feed it with my life, with my blood, and then with a pain at my heart, to tear it from myself and lay it at the feet of the United State.
paras.uz: Bularni yozar ekanman, yonoqlarim yonayotganini sezaman. Balki ayol o'z ichida mitti, ko'zi ochilmagan insonning tomir urishini ilk bor sezganida shunga o'xshash hissiyot kechirar. Bu — men. Ayni paytda bu — men emas. Uzoq oylar davomida uni o'z hayotim, o'z qonim bilan oziqlantirishim, keyin esa yuragim og'rib, uni o'zimdan uzib olib, Yagona Davlat oyoqlari ostiga qo'yishim kerak bo'ladi.

paras.en: Yet I am ready, as everyone, or nearly every one of us, is. I am ready.
paras.uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, men tayyorman. Hamma, yoki deyarli hammamiz kabi, men tayyorman.

chapters.recap_uz: Davlat gazetasida Integral qurilishi tugashi va Raqamlar Yagona Davlatni madh etuvchi asarlar yozishi kerakligi e'lon qilinadi. Integral quruvchisi D-503 shu sababli «Biz» degan qaydlarini yozishni boshlaydi.

chapters.title: Ballet — Square harmony — X

paras.en: Spring. From behind the Green Wall from some unknown plains the wind brings to us the yellow honeyed pollen of flowers. One’s lips are dry from this sweet dust. Every moment one passes one’s tongue over them. Probably, all women whom I meet in the street (and men certainly also), have today sweet lips. This disturbs somewhat my logical thinking. But the sky! The sky is blue. Its limpidness is not marred by a single cloud. (How primitive was the taste of the ancients, since their poets were always inspired by these senseless, formless, stupidly rushing accumulations of steam!) I love, I am sure it will not be an error if I say we love, only such a sky⁠—a sterile, faultless sky. On such days the whole universe seems to be moulded of the same eternal glass, like the Green Wall, and like all our buildings. On such days one sees into the very blue depth of things. One sees their wonderful equations, hitherto unknown. One sees them in everything, even in the most ordinary everyday things.
paras.uz: Bahor. Yashil Devor ortidan, qandaydir noma'lum dashtlardan shamol bizga gullarning sariq, asaldek changini olib keladi. Bu shirin changdan lablar quriydi. Har lahza ularni til bilan yalab qo'yasan. Ehtimol, bugun ko'chada uchratgan barcha ayollarning (va, albatta, erkaklarning ham) lablari shirindir. Bu mantiqiy fikrlashimni biroz bezovta qiladi. Lekin osmon! Osmon moviy. Uning tiniqligini birorta ham bulut buzmaydi. (Qadimgilarning didi qanchalik ibtidoiy bo'lgan, axir ularning shoirlari doim bu ma'nosiz, shaklsiz, ahmoqona yugurgan bug' to'plamlaridan ilhom olishgan!) Men faqat shunday osmonni — steril, beayb osmonni sevaman; ishonchim komilki, «biz sevamiz» desam ham xato bo'lmaydi. Bunday kunlarda butun koinot Yashil Devor kabi, barcha binolarimiz kabi o'sha abadiy shishadan quyilgandek tuyuladi. Bunday kunlarda narsalarning moviy tubini ko'rasan. Ularning shu paytgacha noma'lum ajoyib tenglamalarini ko'rasan. Ularni hamma narsada, hatto eng oddiy kundalik narsalarda ham ko'rasan.

paras.en: Here is an example: this morning I was on the dock where the Integral is being built, and I saw the lathes; blindly, with abandon, the balls of the regulators were rotating; the cranks were swinging from side to side with a glimmer; the working-beam proudly swung its shoulder; and the mechanical chisels were dancing to the melody of an unheard Tarantella. I suddenly perceived all the music, all the beauty, of this colossal, of this mechanical ballet, illumined by light blue rays of sunshine. Then the thought came: why beautiful? Why is a dance beautiful? Answer: because it is an unfree movement. Because the deep meaning of the dance is contained in its absolute, ecstatic submission, in the ideal non-freedom. If it is true that our ancestors would abandon themselves in dancing at the most inspired moments of their lives (religious mysteries, military parades) then it means only one thing: the instinct of non-freedom has been characteristic of human nature from ancient times, and we in our life of today, we are only consciously⁠—
paras.uz: Mana misol: bugun ertalab men Integral qurilayotgan stapelda edim va dastgohlarni ko'rdim: rostlagichlarning sharlari ko'r-ko'rona, o'zini unutib aylanardi; tirsakli vallar yaltirab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa tebranardi; balansir g'urur bilan yelkasini silkitardi; mexanik iskanalar esa eshitilmas tarantella ohangiga raqs tushardi. Men to'satdan quyoshning och moviy nurlari bilan yoritilgan bu ulkan mexanik baletning butun musiqasini, butun go'zalligini his qildim. Keyin fikr keldi: nega go'zal? Raqs nega go'zal? Javob: chunki u erkin bo'lmagan harakat. Chunki raqsning chuqur ma'nosi uning mutlaq, jazavali bo'ysunishida, ideal erksizlikda. Agar ajdodlarimiz hayotlarining eng ilhomli lahzalarida (diniy marosimlar, harbiy paradlar) o'zlarini raqsga berganlari rost bo'lsa, demak bu faqat bitta narsani anglatadi: erksizlik instinkti qadim zamonlardan inson tabiatiga xos bo'lgan, biz esa bugungi hayotimizda faqat ongli ravishda...

paras.en: I was interrupted. The switchboard clicked. I raised my eyes⁠—O-90, of course! In half a minute she herself will be here to take me for the walk.
paras.uz: Gapim bo'lindi. Kommutator chirqilladi. Ko'zlarimni ko'tardim — albatta, O-90! Yarim daqiqadan keyin u o'zi meni sayrga olib ketish uchun shu yerda bo'ladi.

paras.en: Dear O-! She always seems to me to look like her name, O-. She is approximately ten centimeters shorter than the required Maternal Norm. Therefore she appears all round; the rose-colored O of her lips is open to meet every word of mine. She has a round soft dimple on her wrist. Children have such dimples. As she came in, the logical flywheel was still buzzing in my head, and following its inertia, I began to tell her about my new formula which embraced the machines and the dancers and all of us.
paras.uz: Aziz O-! U menga doim o'z ismiga — O-ga o'xshab ko'rinadi. U talab qilingan Onalik Normasidan taxminan o'n santimetr past. Shuning uchun u butunlay yumaloq ko'rinadi; lablarining pushti O harfi mening har bir so'zimni kutib ochiq turadi. Bilagida yumaloq, yumshoq chuqurcha bor. Bolalarda shunday chuqurchalar bo'ladi. U kirganda boshimda mantiqiy maxovik hali ham g'uvullab turardi va uning inersiyasiga ergashib, men unga mashinalarni ham, raqqoslarni ham, hammamizni ham qamrab olgan yangi formulam haqida gapira boshladim.

paras.en: “Wonderful, isn’t it!” I asked.
paras.uz: «Ajoyib, shunday emasmi!» — so'radim men.

paras.en: “Yes, wonderful⁠ ⁠… Spring!” she replied, with a rosy smile.
paras.uz: «Ha, ajoyib... Bahor!» — pushti tabassum bilan javob berdi u.

paras.en: You see? Spring! She talks about Spring! Females!⁠ ⁠… I became silent.
paras.uz: Ko'rdingizmi? Bahor! U bahor haqida gapiryapti! Ayollar!.. Men jim bo'ldim.

paras.en: We were down in the street. The avenue was crowded. On days when the weather is so beautiful the afternoon personal hour is usually the hour of the supplementary walk. As always the big Musical Tower was playing with all its pipes, the March of the United State. The Numbers, hundreds, thousands of Numbers in light blue unifs (probably a derivative of the ancient uniform) with golden badges on the chest⁠—the State number of each one, male or female⁠—the Numbers were walking slowly, four abreast, exaltedly keeping the step. I, we four, were but one of the innumerable waves of a powerful torrent. To my left, O-90 (if one of my long-haired ancestors were writing this a thousand years ago, he would probably call her by that funny word, mine), to my right, two unknown Numbers, a she-Number and a he-Number.
paras.uz: Biz pastda, ko'chada edik. Xiyobon odamga to'la edi. Ob-havo bunchalik go'zal kunlarda tushdan keyingi shaxsiy soat odatda qo'shimcha sayr soati bo'ladi. Har doimgidek katta Musiqa Minorasi barcha quvurlari bilan Yagona Davlat Marshini chalardi. Raqamlar — yuzlab, minglab Raqamlar och moviy yunifalarda (ehtimol, qadimgi «uniforma»ning hosilasi), ko'kraklarida oltin nishonlar — har birining, erkak yoki ayolning davlat raqami — Raqamlar to'rttadan qator bo'lib, hayajon bilan qadamni saqlab sekin yurishardi. Men, biz to'rtovlon, qudratli oqimning son-sanoqsiz to'lqinlaridan biri edik. Chapimda O-90 (agar ming yil oldin sochi uzun ajdodlarimdan biri buni yozganida, uni, ehtimol, o'sha kulgili so'z bilan — «meniki» deb atagan bo'lardi), o'ngimda esa ikki notanish Raqam, bir ayol-Raqam va bir erkak-Raqam.

paras.en: Blue sky, tiny baby suns in each one of our badges; our faces are unclouded by the insanity of thoughts. Rays.⁠ ⁠… Do you picture it? Everything seems to be made of a kind of smiling, a ray-like matter. And the brass measures: Tra-ta-ta-tam.⁠ ⁠… Tra-ta-ta-tam⁠ ⁠… stamping on the brassy steps which sparkle in the sun; with every step you rise higher and higher into the dizzy blue heights.⁠ ⁠… Then, as this morning on the dock, again I saw as if for the first time in my life, the impeccably straight streets, the glistening glass of the pavement, the divine parallelopipeds of the transparent dwellings, the square harmony of the grayish-blue rows of Numbers. And it seemed to me that not past generations, but I myself, had won a victory over the old god and the old life, that I myself had created all this. I felt like a tower: I was afraid to move my elbow, lest the walls, the cupola and the machines should fall to pieces.
paras.uz: Moviy osmon, har birimizning nishonimizda mitti go'dak quyoshlar; yuzlarimizni fikrlar telbaligi xiralashtirmagan. Nurlar... Tasavvur qila olyapsizmi? Hamma narsa qandaydir jilmayuvchi, nurdek moddadan yasalganga o'xshaydi. Mis zarblar esa: Tra-ta-ta-tam... Tra-ta-ta-tam... quyoshda yaltirayotgan mis zinapoyalarni tepib boradi; har qadamda boshni aylantiruvchi moviy balandlikka tobora yuqoriroq ko'tarilasan... Keyin, bugun ertalab stapeldagidek, yana umrimda birinchi marta ko'rgandek beayb to'g'ri ko'chalarni, yo'lkalarning yaltiroq shishasini, shaffof uylarning ilohiy parallelepipedlarini, kulrang-moviy Raqamlar qatorlarining kvadrat uyg'unligini ko'rdim. Va menga eski xudo va eski hayot ustidan o'tgan avlodlar emas, men o'zim g'alaba qozongandek, bularning hammasini men o'zim yaratgandek tuyuldi. Men o'zimni minoradek his qildim: devorlar, gumbaz va mashinalar parchalanib ketmasligi uchun tirsagimni qimirlatishga qo'rqardim.

paras.en: Then without warning⁠—a jump through centuries: I remembered (apparently through an association by contrast) a picture in the museum, a picture of an avenue of the twentieth century, a thundering many-colored confusion of men, wheels, animals, billboards, trees, colors, and birds.⁠ ⁠… They say all this once actually existed!
paras.uz: Keyin ogohlantirishsiz — asrlar osha sakrash: men (aftidan, qarama-qarshilik assotsiatsiyasi orqali) muzeydagi bir suratni esladim, yigirmanchi asr xiyobonining surati — odamlar, g'ildiraklar, hayvonlar, reklama taxtalari, daraxtlar, ranglar va qushlarning gumburlagan rang-barang chalkashligi... Aytishlaricha, bularning hammasi bir paytlar haqiqatan ham mavjud bo'lgan!

paras.en: It seemed to me so incredible, so absurd, that I lost control of myself and laughed aloud. A laugh, as if an echo of mine, reached my ear from the right. I turned. I saw white, very white, sharp teeth, and an unfamiliar female face.
paras.uz: Bu menga shunchalik aql bovar qilmas, shunchalik bema'ni tuyuldiki, o'zimni tutolmay baland ovozda kulib yubordim. O'ng tomondan, go'yo mening kulgimning aks-sadosidek, kulgi qulog'imga yetib keldi. O'girildim. Oppoq, juda oppoq, o'tkir tishlarni va notanish ayol yuzini ko'rdim.

paras.en: “I beg your pardon,” she said, “but you looked about you like an inspired mythological god on the seventh day of creation. You look as though you are sure that I, too, was created by you, by no one but you. It is very flattering.”
paras.uz: «Kechirasiz, — dedi u, — lekin siz atrofga yaratilishning yettinchi kunidagi ilhomlangan afsonaviy xudodek qaradingiz. Go'yo men ham siz tomoningizdan, sizdan boshqa hech kim tomonidan yaratilganimga ishonchingiz komildek ko'rinasiz. Bu juda xushomadli».

paras.en: All this without a smile, even with a certain degree of respect⁠—(she may know that I am the builder of the Integral). In her eyes nevertheless, in her brows, there was a strange irritating X, and I was unable to grasp it, to find an arithmetical expression for it. Somehow I was confused; with a somewhat hazy mind, I tried logically to motivate my laughter.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi tabassumsiz, hatto ma'lum darajada hurmat bilan aytildi — (u mening Integral quruvchisi ekanimni bilishi mumkin). Shunga qaramay, uning ko'zlarida, qoshlarida g'alati, g'ashga tegadigan bir X bor edi va men uni ilg'ab olishga, uning arifmetik ifodasini topishga ojiz edim. Negadir sarosimaga tushdim; biroz chalkash xayol bilan kulgimni mantiqan asoslashga urindim.

paras.en: “It was absolutely clear that this contrast, this impassable abyss, between the things of today and of years ago⁠—”
paras.uz: «Bu qarama-qarshilik, bugungi narsalar bilan qadimgilar o'rtasidagi bu o'tib bo'lmas jarlik mutlaqo aniq edi...»

paras.en: “But why impassable?” (What bright, sharp teeth!) “One might throw a bridge over that abyss. Please imagine: a drum battalion, rows⁠—all this existed before and consequently⁠—”
paras.uz: «Lekin nega o'tib bo'lmas?» (Qanday oq, o'tkir tishlar!) «Bu jarlik ustidan ko'prik tashlash mumkin. Tasavvur qilib ko'ring: baraban batalyoni, qatorlar — bularning hammasi avval ham bo'lgan, demak...»

paras.en: “Oh, yes, it is clear,” I exclaimed.
paras.uz: «Oh, ha, tushunarli!» — xitob qildim men.

paras.en: It was a remarkable intersection of thoughts. She said almost in the same words the things I wrote down before the walk! Do you understand? Even the thoughts! It is because nobody is one, but one of. We are all so much alike⁠—
paras.uz: Bu fikrlarning ajoyib kesishuvi edi. U sayrdan oldin men yozib qo'ygan narsalarni deyarli o'sha so'zlar bilan aytdi! Tushunyapsizmi? Hatto fikrlar ham! Chunki hech kim «bitta» emas, balki «bittasi». Biz hammamiz shunchalik o'xshashmiz...

paras.en: “Are you sure?” I noticed her brows which rose to the temples in an acute angle⁠—like the sharp corners of an X. Again I was confused, casting a glance to the right, then to the left. To my right⁠—she, slender, abrupt, resistantly flexible like a whip, I-330 (I saw her number now). To my left, O-, totally different, made all of circles with a childlike dimple on her wrist; and at the very end of our row, an unknown he-Number, double-curved like the letter S. We were all so different from one another.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: «Ishonchingiz komilmi?» Men uning chakkalariga qadar o'tkir burchak bilan ko'tarilgan qoshlarini payqadim — X harfining o'tkir uchlaridek. Yana sarosimaga tushib, o'ngga, keyin chapga qaradim. O'ngimda — u, qiltiriq, keskin, qamchidek qayishqoq va qarshilik ko'rsatuvchi, I-330 (endi uning raqamini ko'rdim). Chapimda O-, butunlay boshqacha, butunlay aylanalardan yasalgan, bilagida bolalarnikidek chuqurcha; qatorimizning eng chetida esa S harfidek ikki marta egilgan notanish erkak-Raqam. Biz hammamiz bir-birimizdan shunchalik farq qilardik...

paras.en: The one to my right, I-330, apparently caught my confused eye, for she said with a sigh, “Yes, alas!”
paras.uz: O'ngimdagi I-330, aftidan, mening sarosimali nigohimni ilg'adi, chunki u xo'rsinib dedi: «Ha, afsus!»

paras.en: I don’t deny that this exclamation was quite in place, but again there was something in her face or in her voice.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Bu xitob o'rinli bo'lganini inkor etmayman, lekin yana uning yuzida yoki ovozida nimadir bor edi...

paras.en: With an abruptness unusual for me, I said, “Why ‘alas’? Science is developing and if not now, then within fifty or one hundred years⁠—”
paras.uz: Men uchun g'ayrioddiy keskinlik bilan dedim: «Nega "afsus"? Fan rivojlanmoqda va hozir bo'lmasa ham, ellik yoki yuz yildan keyin...»

paras.en: “Even the noses will⁠—”
paras.uz: «Hatto burunlar ham...»

paras.en: “Yes, noses!” This time I almost shouted, “Since there is still a reason, no matter what, for envy.⁠ ⁠… Since my nose is button-like and someone else’s is⁠—”
paras.uz: «Ha, burunlar! — bu safar deyarli qichqirdim. — Hasad uchun hali ham sabab bor ekan, qanday sabab bo'lmasin... Mening burnim tugmachadek, boshqa birovniki esa...»

paras.en: “Well your nose is rather classic, as they would say in the ancient days, although your hands⁠—No, no, show me your hands!”
paras.uz: «Burningiz qadimgi kunlarda aytganlaridek ancha klassik, lekin qo'llaringiz... Yo'q, yo'q, qo'llaringizni ko'rsating!»

paras.en: I hate to have anyone look at my hands; they are covered with long hair⁠—a stupid atavism. I stretched out my hand and said as indifferently as I could, “Apelike.”
paras.uz: Birov qo'llarimga qarashini yomon ko'raman: ular uzun tuklar bilan qoplangan — ahmoqona atavizm. Qo'limni uzatdim va iloji boricha befarq ohangda dedim: «Maymunnikidek».

paras.en: She glanced at my hand, then at my face.
paras.uz: U qo'limga, keyin yuzimga qaradi.

paras.en: “No, a very curious harmony.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, juda qiziq uyg'unlik».

paras.en: She weighed me with her eyes as though with scales. The little horns again appeared at the corners of her brows.
paras.uz: U meni ko'zlari bilan go'yo tarozida tortib ko'rdi. Qoshlarining uchlarida yana kichkina shoxchalar paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: “He is registered in my name,” exclaimed O-90 with a rosy smile.
paras.uz: «U mening nomimga yozilgan», — pushti tabassum bilan xitob qildi O-90.

paras.en: I made a grimace. Strictly speaking, she was out of order. This dear O-, how shall I say it? the speed of her tongue is not correctly calculated; the speed per second of her tongue should be slightly less than the speed per second of her thoughts⁠—at any rate not the reverse.
paras.uz: Men aftimni burishtirdim. Aslini olganda, u o'rinsiz gapirdi. Bu aziz O-ning, qanday aytsam ekan, tilining tezligi to'g'ri hisoblanmagan; tilining soniyadagi tezligi fikrlarining soniyadagi tezligidan biroz kam bo'lishi kerak — har holda aksincha emas.

paras.en: At the end of the avenue the big bell of the Accumulating Tower resounded seventeen. The personal hour was at an end. I-330 was leaving us with that S-like he-Number. He has such a respectable, and I noticed then, such a familiar face. I must have met him somewhere, but where I could not remember. Upon leaving me I-330 said with the same X-like smile:
paras.uz: Xiyobon oxirida Jamg'arma Minorasining katta qo'ng'irog'i o'n yetti marta jarangladi. Shaxsiy soat tugadi. I-330 o'sha S-simon erkak-Raqam bilan bizdan ketayotgan edi. Uning yuzi shunchalik hurmatli, men o'shanda payqadimki, shunchalik tanish edi. Uni qayerdadir uchratgan bo'lsam kerak, lekin qayerda — eslay olmadim. Xayrlashayotganda I-330 o'sha X-simon tabassum bilan dedi:

paras.en: “Drop in day after tomorrow at auditorium 112.”
paras.uz: «Indinga 112-auditoriyaga kirib o'ting».

paras.en: I shrugged my shoulders: “If I am assigned to the auditorium you just named⁠—”
paras.uz: Men yelka qisdim: «Agar menga siz aytgan auditoriyaga naryad berilsa...»

paras.en: She, with a peculiar, incomprehensible certainty: “You will.”
paras.uz: U qandaydir g'alati, tushunib bo'lmas ishonch bilan: «Beriladi».

paras.en: The woman had upon me a disagreeable effect, like an irrational component of an equation which you cannot eliminate. I was glad to remain alone with dear O-, at least for a short while. Hand in hand with her, I passed four lines of avenues; at the next corner she went to the right, I to the left. O- timidly raised her round blue crystalline eyes:
paras.uz: Bu ayol menga tenglamaning yo'qotib bo'lmaydigan irratsional hadi kabi yoqimsiz ta'sir qildi. Aziz O- bilan hech bo'lmaganda qisqa vaqt yolg'iz qolganimdan xursand edim. Qo'l ushlashib, biz to'rtta xiyobondan o'tdik; keyingi burchakda u o'ngga, men chapga burildim. O- yumaloq moviy billur ko'zlarini tortinib ko'tardi:

paras.en: “I would like so much to come to you today and pull down the curtains, especially today, right now.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: «Bugun sizning oldingizga borib, pardalarni tushirishni shunchalik xohlardim, ayniqsa bugun, hozirning o'zida...»

paras.en: How funny she is. But what could I say to her? She was with me only yesterday and she knows as well as I that our next sexual day is day-after-tomorrow. It is merely another case in which her thoughts are too far ahead. It sometimes happens that the spark comes too early to the motor.
paras.uz: Qanday kulgili u. Lekin men unga nima deya olardim? U kechagina men bilan edi va keyingi jinsiy kunimiz indinga ekanini men kabi biladi. Bu uning fikrlari haddan tashqari oldinga ketishining yana bir holati, xolos. Ba'zan dvigatelga uchqun juda erta keladi.

paras.en: At parting I kissed her twice⁠—no, I shall be exact, three times, on her wonderful blue eyes, such clear, unclouded eyes.
paras.uz: Xayrlashayotganda men uning ajoyib moviy ko'zlaridan, shunday tiniq, bulutsiz ko'zlaridan ikki marta — yo'q, aniq bo'lay, uch marta o'pdim.

…me: why beautiful? Why is a dance beautiful? Answer: because it is an unfree movement. Because the deep meaning of the dance is contained in its absolute, ecsta…
…er of each one, male or female⁠—the Numbers were walking slowly, four abreast, exaltedly keeping the step. I, we four, were but one of the innumerable waves of…
The woman had upon me a disagreeable effect, like an irrational component of an equation which you cannot eliminate. I was glad to remain alone…
…ached my ear from the right. I turned. I saw white, very white, sharp teeth, and an unfamiliar female face.

quiz.q: Why does D-503 think dance is beautiful?
quiz.why_uz: Uning fikricha, raqsning go'zalligi to'liq bo'ysunish va erksizlikda.

quiz.q: Whom does D-503 meet for the first time on the walk?
quiz.why_uz: I-330 — o'tkir tishli, qoshlarida «X» bor ayol.

chapters.recap_uz: Bahorgi sayrda D-503 O-90 bilan yuradi va birinchi marta I-330 ni uchratadi. Uning o'tkir tishlari va qoshlaridagi «X» D-503 ni bezovta qiladi.

chapters.title: A coat — A wall — The tables

paras.en: I looked over all that I wrote down yesterday and I find that my descriptions are not sufficiently clear. That is, everything would undoubtedly be clear to one of us but who knows to whom my Integral will some day bring these records? Perhaps you, like our ancestors, have read the great book of civilization only up to the page of nine hundred years ago. Perhaps you don’t know even such elementary things as the Hour Tables, Personal Hours, Maternal Norm, Green Wall, Well-Doer. It seems droll to me and at the same time very difficult, to explain these things. It is as though, let us say, a writer of the twentieth century should start to explain in his novel such words as coat, apartment, wife. Yet if his novel had been translated for primitive races, how could he have avoided explaining what a coat meant? I am sure that the primitive man would look at a coat and think, “What is this for? It is only a burden, an unnecessary burden.” I am sure that you will feel the same, if I tell you that not one of us has ever stepped beyond the Green Wall since the Two Hundred Years’ War.
paras.uz: Kecha yozganlarimning hammasini ko'zdan kechirdim va tasvirlarim yetarlicha aniq emasligini ko'rdim. Ya'ni, bizdan har biri uchun hammasi, shubhasiz, aniq bo'lardi, lekin Integralim bu qaydlarni qachondir kimga olib borishini kim biladi? Ehtimol, siz ham ajdodlarimiz kabi sivilizatsiyaning buyuk kitobini faqat to'qqiz yuz yil oldingi sahifasigacha o'qigansiz. Ehtimol, siz hatto Soatlar Jadvali, Shaxsiy Soatlar, Onalik Normasi, Yashil Devor, Homiy kabi oddiy narsalarni ham bilmassiz. Bu narsalarni tushuntirish menga kulgili va shu bilan birga juda qiyin tuyuladi. Bu go'yo, aytaylik, yigirmanchi asr yozuvchisi o'z romanida «palto», «kvartira», «xotin» kabi so'zlarni tushuntira boshlagandek. Lekin agar uning romani ibtidoiy xalqlar uchun tarjima qilinganida, palto nima ekanini tushuntirmasdan qanday qutula olardi? Ishonchim komilki, ibtidoiy odam paltoga qarab: «Bu nima uchun? Bu shunchaki yuk, keraksiz yuk» deb o'ylardi. Ishonchim komilki, agar Ikki Yuz Yillik Urushdan beri birortamiz ham Yashil Devordan nariga qadam qo'ymaganini aytsam, siz ham xuddi shunday his qilasiz.

paras.en: But, dear readers, you must think, at least a little. It helps.
paras.uz: Lekin, aziz o'quvchilar, siz hech bo'lmaganda ozgina o'ylashingiz kerak. Bu yordam beradi.

paras.en: It is clear that the history of mankind as far as our knowledge goes, is a history of the transition from nomadic forms to more sedentary ones. Does it not follow that the most sedentary form of life (ours) is at the same time, the most perfect one? There was a time when people were rushing from one end of the earth to another, but this was the prehistoric time when such things as nations, wars, commerce, different discoveries of different Americas still existed. Who has need of these things now?
paras.uz: Aniqki, insoniyat tarixi, bilganimizcha, ko'chmanchi shakllardan o'troqroq shakllarga o'tish tarixi. Bundan hayotning eng o'troq shakli (bizniki) ayni paytda eng mukammali ekani kelib chiqmaydimi? Odamlar yerning bir chetidan ikkinchisiga yugurib yurgan zamon bo'lgan, lekin bu millatlar, urushlar, savdo, turli Amerikalarning turli kashfiyotlari hali mavjud bo'lgan tarixdan oldingi zamon edi. Endi bularga kimning ehtiyoji bor?

paras.en: I admit humanity acquired this habit of a sedentary form of life not without difficulty and not at once. When the Two Hundred Years’ War had destroyed all the roads which later were overgrown with grass, it was probably very difficult at first. It seemed uncomfortable to live in cities which were cut off from each other by green debris. But what of it? Man soon after he lost his tail probably did not learn at once how to chase away flies without its help. I am almost sure that at first he was even lonesome without his tail, but now, can you imagine yourself with a tail? Or can you imagine yourself walking in the street naked, without clothes? (It is possible you go without clothes still.) Here we have the same case. I cannot imagine a city which is not clad with a Green Wall; I cannot imagine a life which is not clad with the figures of our Tables.
paras.uz: Tan olaman, insoniyat o'troq hayot shakliga bu odatni osonlikcha va birdaniga orttirmagan. Ikki Yuz Yillik Urush keyinchalik o't bosib ketgan barcha yo'llarni vayron qilganda, avvaliga, ehtimol, juda qiyin bo'lgan. Bir-biridan yashil chakalakzor bilan uzilgan shaharlarda yashash noqulay tuyulgan. Lekin nima bo'pti? Inson dumini yo'qotgandan keyin, ehtimol, pashshalarni usiz haydashni birdaniga o'rganmagan. Deyarli aminmanki, avvaliga u dumsiz hatto zerikkan ham, lekin endi o'zingizni dumli tasavvur qila olasizmi? Yoki ko'chada yalang'och, kiyimsiz yurganingizni tasavvur qila olasizmi? (Ehtimol, siz hali ham kiyimsiz yurarsiz.) Bu yerda ham xuddi shunday. Men Yashil Devor bilan kiyintirilmagan shaharni tasavvur qila olmayman; Jadvalimiz raqamlari bilan kiyintirilmagan hayotni tasavvur qila olmayman.

paras.en: Tables.⁠ ⁠… Now even, purple figures look at me austerely yet kindly from the golden background of the wall. Involuntarily I am reminded of the thing which was called by the ancients, “Sainted Image,” and I feel a desire to compose verses, or prayers which are the same. Oh, why am not I a poet, so as to be able properly to glorify the Tables, the heart and pulse of the United State!
paras.uz: Jadval... Hozir ham devordagi oltin fondan binafsha raqamlar menga qattiq, ammo mehribon qarab turibdi. Beixtiyor qadimgilar «ikona» deb atagan narsa yodimga tushadi va she'r yoki, xuddi shu narsa bo'lgan, duo yozgim keladi. Oh, nega men shoir emasman, Yagona Davlatning yuragi va tomir urishi bo'lgan Jadvalni munosib ulug'lay olishim uchun!

paras.en: All of us and perhaps all of you read in childhood while in school, that greatest of all monuments of ancient literature, the Official Railroad Guide. But if you compare this with the Tables, you will see side by side graphite and diamonds. Both are the same, carbon. But how eternal, transparent, how shining the diamond! Who does not lose his breath when he runs through the pages of the Guide? The Tables transformed each one of us, actually, into a six-wheeled steel hero of a great poem. Every morning with six-wheeled precision, at the same hour, at the same minute, we wake up, millions of us at once. At the very same hour millions like one we begin our work, and millions like one, we finish it. United into a single body with a million hands, at the very same second, designated by the Tables, we carry the spoons to our mouths; at the same second we all go out to walk, go to the auditorium, to the halls for the Taylor exercises and then to bed.
paras.uz: Hammamiz va, ehtimol, sizlar ham bolaligimizda maktabda qadimiy adabiyotning eng buyuk yodgorligi — «Temir yo'l jadvali»ni o'qiganmiz. Lekin agar uni Jadval bilan solishtirsangiz, yonma-yon grafit va olmosni ko'rasiz. Ikkalasi ham bir xil — uglerod. Lekin olmos qanchalik abadiy, shaffof, qanchalik yaltiroq! «Temir yo'l jadvali» sahifalarini varaqlayotganda kimning nafasi tiqilmaydi? Jadval esa har birimizni haqiqatan ham buyuk dostonning olti g'ildirakli po'lat qahramoniga aylantirdi. Har kuni ertalab olti g'ildirakli aniqlik bilan, bir soatda, bir daqiqada biz millionlab odam birdaniga uyg'onamiz. Aynan bir soatda millionlab odam bir kishidek ishni boshlaymiz va millionlab odam bir kishidek tugatamiz. Million qo'lli yagona tanaga birlashib, Jadval belgilagan aynan bir soniyada qoshiqlarni og'zimizga olib boramiz; bir soniyada hammamiz sayrga chiqamiz, auditoriyaga, Teylor mashqlari zallariga boramiz va keyin uxlashga yotamiz.

paras.en: I shall be quite frank: even we have not attained the absolute, exact solution of the problem of happiness. Twice a day, from sixteen to seventeen o’clock and from twenty-one to twenty-two, our united powerful organism dissolves into separate cells; these are the personal hours designated by the Tables. During these hours you would see the curtains discreetly drawn in the rooms of some; others march slowly over the pavement of the main avenue or sit at their desks as I sit now. But I firmly believe, let them call me an idealist and a dreamer, I believe that sooner or later we shall somehow find even for these hours, a place in the general formula. Somehow, all of the 86,400 seconds will be incorporated in the Tables of Hours.
paras.uz: Men butunlay ochiq bo'laman: hatto biz ham baxt muammosining mutlaq, aniq yechimiga erishmaganmiz. Kuniga ikki marta, soat o'n oltidan o'n yettigacha va yigirma birdan yigirma ikkigacha, birlashgan qudratli organizmimiz alohida hujayralarga bo'linadi; bular Jadval belgilagan Shaxsiy Soatlar. Bu soatlarda siz ba'zilarning xonalarida pardalar odob bilan tushirilganini ko'rasiz; boshqalar asosiy xiyobon yo'lkasi bo'ylab sekin qadam tashlaydi yoki hozir men o'tirganimdek stollari yonida o'tiradi. Lekin men qat'iy ishonaman — mayli, meni idealist va xayolparast deyishsin — ishonamanki, ertami-kechmi biz bu soatlar uchun ham umumiy formulada joy topamiz. Qandaydir yo'l bilan barcha 86 400 soniya Soatlar Jadvaliga kiritiladi.

paras.en: I have had opportunity to read and hear many improbable things about those times when human beings still lived in the state of freedom, that is, an unorganized primitive state. One thing has always seemed to me the most improbable: how could a government, even a primitive government, permit people to live without anything like our Tables⁠—without compulsory walks, without precise regulation of the time to eat, for instance? They would get up and go to bed whenever they liked. Some historians even say that in those days the streets were lighted all night; and all night people went about the streets.
paras.uz: Odamlar hali erkinlik holatida, ya'ni uyushmagan ibtidoiy holatda yashagan zamonlar haqida ko'p aql bovar qilmas narsalarni o'qish va eshitishga imkonim bo'lgan. Bir narsa menga doim eng aql bovar qilmas tuyulgan: qanday qilib hukumat, hatto ibtidoiy hukumat ham, odamlarga Jadvalimizga o'xshash hech narsasiz — majburiy sayrlarsiz, masalan, ovqatlanish vaqtini aniq tartibga solmasdan yashashga ruxsat bera olgan? Ular xohlagan paytda turib, xohlagan paytda yotishardi. Ba'zi tarixchilar hatto o'sha kunlarda ko'chalar tun bo'yi yoritilganini va odamlar tun bo'yi ko'chalarda yurganini aytishadi.

paras.en: That I cannot understand; true, their minds were rather limited in those days. Yet they should have understood, should they not, that such a life was actually wholesale murder, although slow murder, day after day? The State (humanitarianism) forbade in those days the murder of one person, but it did not forbid the killing of millions slowly and by half. To kill one, that is, to reduce the general sum of human life by fifty years, was considered criminal, but to reduce the general sum of human life by fifty million years was not considered criminal! Is it not droll? Today this simple mathematical moral problem could easily be solved in half a minute’s time by any ten-year-old Number, yet they couldn’t do it! All their Immanuel Kants together couldn’t do it! It didn’t enter the heads of all their Kants to build a system of scientific ethics, that is, ethics based on adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing.
paras.uz: Buni tushuna olmayman; to'g'ri, o'sha kunlarda ularning aqli ancha cheklangan edi. Lekin ular bunday hayot aslida ommaviy qotillik, sekin bo'lsa ham, kundan-kunga qotillik ekanini tushunishlari kerak edi-ku, shunday emasmi? O'sha kunlarda Davlat (insonparvarlik) bir kishini o'ldirishni man qilgan, lekin millionlab odamlarni sekin va yarimta o'ldirishni man qilmagan. Bir kishini o'ldirish, ya'ni inson hayotining umumiy yig'indisini ellik yilga kamaytirish jinoyat hisoblangan, lekin inson hayotining umumiy yig'indisini ellik million yilga kamaytirish jinoyat hisoblanmagan! Kulgili emasmi? Bugun bu oddiy matematik-axloqiy masalani har qanday o'n yoshli Raqam yarim daqiqada osongina yecha oladi, ular esa yecha olishmagan! Ularning hamma Immanuil Kantlari birgalikda ham yecha olishmagan! Ularning hamma Kantlarining boshiga ilmiy axloq tizimini, ya'ni qo'shish, ayirish, ko'paytirish va bo'lishga asoslangan axloqni qurish kelmagan.

paras.en: Further, is it not absurd that their State (they called it State!) left sexual life absolutely without control? However, whenever and as much as they wanted.⁠ ⁠… Absolutely unscientific like beasts; and like beasts they blindly gave birth to children! Is it not strange to understand gardening, chicken-farming, fishery (we have definite knowledge that they were familiar with all these things), and not to be able to reach the last step in this logical scale, namely, production of children⁠—not to be able to discover such things as Maternal and Paternal Norms?
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, ularning davlati (ular uni davlat deb atashgan!) jinsiy hayotni mutlaqo nazoratsiz qoldirgani bema'ni emasmi? Qanday xohlasa, qachon xohlasa va qancha xohlasa... Mutlaqo ilmsiz, hayvonlardek; va hayvonlardek ko'r-ko'rona bola tug'ishgan! Bog'dorchilik, parrandachilik, baliqchilikni tushunish (biz ular bularning hammasini bilganini aniq bilamiz) va bu mantiqiy zinapoyaning oxirgi pog'onasiga — bola ishlab chiqarishga yeta olmaslik, Onalik va Otalik Normalari kabi narsalarni kashf eta olmaslik g'alati emasmi?

paras.en: It is so droll, so improbable, that while I write this I am afraid lest you, my unknown future readers, should think I am merely a bad jester. I feel almost as though you may think I simply want to mock you and with a most serious appearance try to relate to you absolute nonsense. But first, I am incapable of jesting, for in every joke a lie has its hidden function. And second, the science of the United State contends that the life of the ancients was exactly what I am describing, and the science of the United State cannot make a mistake! Yet how could they have State logic, since they lived in a condition of freedom like beasts, like apes, like herds? What could one expect of them, since even in our day one hears from time to time, coming from the bottom, the primitive depths, the echo of the apes?
paras.uz: Bu shunchalik kulgili, shunchalik aql bovar qilmaski, buni yozayotganda men, noma'lum kelajakdagi o'quvchilarim, sizlar meni shunchaki yomon masxaraboz deb o'ylashingizdan qo'rqaman. Go'yo siz meni shunchaki sizni masxara qilmoqchi va eng jiddiy qiyofada sizga mutlaq bema'nilikni aytib bermoqchi deb o'ylashingiz mumkindek his qilaman. Lekin birinchidan, men hazillashishga qodir emasman, chunki har bir hazilda yolg'on yashirin vazifa bajaradi. Ikkinchidan, Yagona Davlat fani qadimgilarning hayoti aynan men tasvirlayotgandek bo'lganini ta'kidlaydi, Yagona Davlat fani esa xato qila olmaydi! Lekin ular hayvonlardek, maymunlardek, podalardek erkinlik holatida yashagan ekan, qanday qilib davlat mantig'iga ega bo'la olishardi? Hatto bizning kunlarimizda ham vaqti-vaqti bilan tubdan, ibtidoiy chuqurliklardan maymunlarning aks-sadosi eshitilib turar ekan, ulardan nimani kutish mumkin edi?

paras.en: Fortunately it happens only from time to time, very seldom. Happily it is only a case of small parts breaking; these may easily be repaired without stopping the eternal great march of the whole machine. And in order to eliminate a broken peg we have the skillful heavy hand of the Well-Doer, we have the experienced eyes of the Guardians.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Baxtimizga, bu faqat vaqti-vaqti bilan, juda kamdan-kam bo'ladi. Baxtimizga, bu faqat mayda qismlar sinishi holati; ularni butun mashinaning abadiy buyuk harakatini to'xtatmasdan osongina tuzatish mumkin. Singan murvatni chiqarib tashlash uchun bizda Homiyning mohir og'ir qo'li bor, Qo'riqchilarning tajribali ko'zlari bor...

paras.en: By the way, I just thought of that Number whom I met yesterday, the double-curved one like the letter S; I think I have seen him several times coming out of the Bureau of the Guardians. Now I understand why I felt such an instinctive respect for him and a kind of awkwardness when that strange I-330 at his side.⁠ ⁠… I must confess that, that I⁠—⁠ ⁠… they ring the bell, time to sleep, it is twenty-two-thirty. Till tomorrow, then.
paras.uz: Aytgancha, hozirgina kecha uchratgan o'sha Raqam, S harfidek ikki marta egilgani esimga tushdi; menimcha, uning Qo'riqchilar Idorasidan chiqayotganini bir necha marta ko'rganman. Endi tushunaman, nega unga nisbatan bunday instinktiv hurmat va o'sha g'alati I-330 uning yonida bo'lganda qandaydir noqulaylik his qildim... Tan olishim kerakki, men... qo'ng'iroq chalinyapti, uxlash vaqti, soat yigirma ikki o'ttiz. Unday bo'lsa, ertagacha.

quiz.why_uz: Shahar Yashil Devor bilan o'ralgan va undan tashqariga hech kim chiqmaydi.

o: During two personal hours a day
quiz.why_uz: Kuniga ikki marta — 16–17 va 21–22 da — shaxsiy soatlar bor.

chapters.recap_uz: D-503 kelajakdagi o'quvchiga Soatlar Jadvali, Shaxsiy Soatlar va Yashil Devor nima ekanini tushuntiradi. U erkinlik va tartibsizlikni qadimgilarning ahmoqligi deb hisoblaydi.

chapters.title: The wild man with a barometer — Epilepsy — If

paras.en: Until today everything in life seemed to me clear (that is why, I think, I always had a sort of partiality toward the word “clear”), but today⁠ ⁠… I don’t understand. First, I really was assigned to auditorium 112 as she said, although the probability was as 500:10,000,000 or 1:20,000. (500 is the number of auditoriums and there are 10,000,000 Numbers.) And second⁠ ⁠… but let me relate things in successive order. The auditorium: an enormous half-globe of glass with the sun piercing through. The circular rows of noble, globe-like, closely-shaven heads. With joy in my heart I looked around. I believe I was looking in the hope of seeing the rose-colored scythe, the dear lips of O-, somewhere among the blue waves of the unifs. Then I saw extraordinarily white, sharp teeth like the.⁠ ⁠… But no! Tonight at twenty-one o’clock O- was to come to me; therefore my desire to see her was quite natural. The bell. We stood up, sang the Hymn of the United State, and our clever phono-lecturer appeared on the platform with a sparkling golden megaphone.
paras.uz: Bugungacha hayotda hamma narsa menga aniq tuyulardi (menimcha, shuning uchun ham «aniq» so'ziga doim qandaydir moyilligim bor edi), lekin bugun... tushunmayapman. Birinchidan, menga haqiqatan ham u aytganidek 112-auditoriyaga naryad berildi, garchi ehtimollik 500:10 000 000 yoki 1:20 000 bo'lsa ham. (500 — auditoriyalar soni, Raqamlar esa 10 000 000.) Ikkinchidan esa... lekin voqealarni ketma-ket aytib beray. Auditoriya: quyosh teshib o'tayotgan ulkan shisha yarimshar. Olijanob, shardek, taqir qirilgan boshlarning doira qatorlari. Qalbimda quvonch bilan atrofga qaradim. Menimcha, yunifalarning moviy to'lqinlari orasida qayerdadir pushti o'roqni, O-ning aziz lablarini ko'rish umidida qaragandim. Keyin g'ayrioddiy oq, o'tkir tishlarni ko'rdim, xuddi... Lekin yo'q! Bugun kechqurun soat yigirma birda O- mening oldimga kelishi kerak edi; shuning uchun uni ko'rish istagim mutlaqo tabiiy edi. Qo'ng'iroq. Biz o'rnimizdan turdik, Yagona Davlat Madhiyasini kuyladik va minbarda yaltiroq oltin karnay bilan aqlli fonolektorimiz paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: “Respected Numbers, not so long ago our archaeologists dug up a book written in the twentieth century. In this book the ironical author tells about a Wild Man and a barometer. The Wild Man noticed that every time the barometer’s hand stopped on the word ‘rain,’ it actually rained. And as the Wild Man craved rain, he let out as much mercury as was necessary to put it at the level of the word ‘rain’ (on the screen a Wild Man with feathers, letting out the mercury. Laughter).
paras.uz: «Hurmatli Raqamlar, yaqinda arxeologlarimiz yigirmanchi asrda yozilgan bir kitobni qazib topishdi. Bu kitobda kinoyachi muallif Yovvoyi va barometr haqida hikoya qiladi. Yovvoyi har safar barometr mili "yomg'ir" so'zida to'xtaganda haqiqatan ham yomg'ir yog'ishini payqagan. Yovvoyi yomg'irni juda xohlagani uchun, milni "yomg'ir" darajasiga keltirish uchun kerak bo'lgancha simobni chiqarib tashlagan (ekranda patlar taqqan Yovvoyi simobni chiqarmoqda. Kulgi).

paras.en: “You are laughing at him, but don’t you think the ‘European’ of that age deserves more to be laughed at? He, like the Wild Man, wanted rain⁠—rain with a little r, an algebraic rain; but he remained standing before the barometer like a wet hen. The Wild Man at least had more courage and energy and logic, although primitive logic. The Wild Man showed the ability to establish a connection between cause and effect: by letting out the mercury he made the first step on the path which.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: Siz uning ustidan kulyapsiz, lekin o'sha davrning "yevropalig'i" ko'proq kulgiga loyiq deb o'ylamaysizmi? U ham Yovvoyi kabi yomg'irni — kichik harfli yomg'irni, algebraik yomg'irni xohlagan; lekin u barometr oldida ho'l tovuqdek turib qolgan. Yovvoyida hech bo'lmaganda ko'proq jasorat, g'ayrat va mantiq bor edi, garchi ibtidoiy mantiq bo'lsa ham. Yovvoyi sabab va oqibat o'rtasida bog'liqlik o'rnatish qobiliyatini ko'rsatdi: simobni chiqarib, u yo'lda birinchi qadamni tashladi, u yo'l esa...»

paras.en: Here (I repeat, I am not concealing anything, I am setting down everything) I suddenly became impermeable to the quickening currents coming from the megaphone. I suddenly felt I had come here in vain (why in vain and how could I not have come here, where I was assigned?). Everything seemed to me empty like a shell. I succeeded with difficulty in switching my attention in again when the phono-lecturer came to the main theme of the evening⁠—to our music as a mathematical composition (mathematics is the cause, music the effect). The phono-lecturer began the description of the recently invented musicometer.
paras.uz: Shu yerda (takrorlayman, men hech narsani yashirmayapman, hammasini yozib boryapman) men to'satdan karnaydan kelayotgan jonlantiruvchi oqimlarga o'tkazmaydigan bo'lib qoldim. To'satdan bu yerga behuda kelgandek his qildim (nega behuda va menga naryad berilgan joyga qanday kelmasligim mumkin edi?). Hamma narsa menga chig'anoqdek bo'm-bo'sh tuyuldi. Fonolektor kechaning asosiy mavzusiga — musiqamizga matematik kompozitsiya sifatida (matematika — sabab, musiqa — oqibat) o'tganda, e'tiborimni yana zo'rg'a ulay oldim. Fonolektor yaqinda ixtiro qilingan musiqometrni tasvirlay boshladi.

paras.en: “… By merely rotating this handle anyone is enabled to produce about three sonatas per hour. What difficulties our predecessors had in making music! They were able to compose only by bringing themselves to strokes of inspiration⁠—an extinct form of epilepsy. Here you have an amusing illustration of their achievements: the music of Scriabin, twentieth century. This black box,” (a curtain parted on the platform, and we saw an ancient instrument) “this box they called the ‘Royal Grand.’ They attached to this the idea of regality, which also goes to prove how their music.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: «...Shunchaki bu dastakni aylantirish bilan har kim soatiga uchtagacha sonata yarata oladi. Ajdodlarimiz musiqa yaratishda qanday qiyinchiliklarga duch kelishgan! Ular faqat o'zlarini "ilhom" xurujlariga — epilepsiyaning yo'qolib ketgan bir shakliga keltirish orqali bastalay olishgan. Mana ularning yutuqlariga kulgili misol: Skryabin musiqasi, yigirmanchi asr. Bu qora quti, — (minbardagi parda ochildi va biz qadimiy cholg'uni ko'rdik) — bu qutini ular "royal", ya'ni "qirollik" deb atashgan. Ular unga qirollik g'oyasini bog'lashgan, bu ham ularning musiqasi qanchalik...»

paras.en: And I don’t remember anything further. Very possibly because⁠ ⁠… I’ll tell you frankly, because she, I-330, came to the “Royal” box. Probably I was simply startled by her unexpected appearance on the platform.
paras.uz: Undan keyingisini eslay olmayman. Ehtimol, chunki... ochig'ini aytaman, chunki u, I-330, «royal» qutisi oldiga keldi. Ehtimol, men shunchaki uning minbarda kutilmaganda paydo bo'lishidan cho'chib ketgandirman.

paras.en: She was dressed in a fantastic dress of the ancient time, a black dress closely fitting the body, sharply delimiting the white of her shoulders and breast and that warm shadow waving with her breath between.⁠ ⁠… And the dazzling, almost angry teeth. A smile, a bite, directed downward. She took her seat; she began to play something wild, convulsive, loud like all their life then⁠—not a shadow of rational mechanism. Of course all those around me were right; they were laughing. Only a few⁠ ⁠… but why is it that I too, I⁠ ⁠… ?
paras.uz: U qadimiy zamonning g'aroyib libosida edi — tanaga qattiq yopishgan qora ko'ylakda, u yelkalari va ko'kragining oqligini va ular orasida nafasi bilan tebranib turgan o'sha iliq soyani keskin ajratib turardi... Va ko'zni qamashtiruvchi, deyarli g'azabli tishlar. Tabassum, pastga qaratilgan tishlash. U o'tirdi; u qandaydir yovvoyi, tutqanoqli, baland, ularning o'sha paytdagi butun hayoti kabi — oqilona mexanizmning soyasi ham bo'lmagan narsani chala boshladi. Albatta, atrofimdagilarning hammasi haq edi; ular kulishardi. Faqat bir nechtasi... lekin nega men ham, men...?

paras.en: Yes, epilepsy, a mental disease, a pain. A slow, sweet pain, bite, and it goes deeper and becomes sharper. And then, slowly, sunshine⁠—not our sunshine, not crystalline, bluish and soft, coming through the glass bricks. No, a wild sunshine, rushing and burning, tearing everything into small bits.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Ha, epilepsiya, ruhiy kasallik, og'riq. Sekin, shirin og'riq, tishlash, u tobora chuqurlashib, o'tkirlashib boradi. Keyin sekin quyosh — bizning quyoshimiz emas, shisha g'ishtlar orqali keladigan billur, moviy va yumshoq quyosh emas. Yo'q, yovvoyi, shitob bilan otilayotgan, kuydiruvchi, hamma narsani mayda parchalarga yirtuvchi quyosh...

paras.en: The Number at my left glanced at me and chuckled. I don’t know why but I remember exactly how a microscopic saliva bubble appeared on his lips and burst. That bubble brought me back to myself. I was again I.
paras.uz: Chapimdagi Raqam menga qarab kuldi. Nima uchunligini bilmayman, lekin uning lablarida mikroskopik so'lak pufakchasi paydo bo'lib, yorilganini aniq eslayman. O'sha pufakcha meni o'zimga qaytardi. Men yana men edim.

paras.en: Like all the other Numbers I heard now only the senseless, disorderly cracking of the chords. I laughed; I felt so light and simple. The gifted phono-lecturer represented to us only too well that wild epoch. And that was all.
paras.uz: Boshqa barcha Raqamlar kabi endi men ham faqat akkordlarning ma'nosiz, tartibsiz shaqirlashini eshitardim. Kuldim; o'zimni shunchalik yengil va sodda his qildim. Iste'dodli fonolektor bizga o'sha yovvoyi davrni juda yaxshi ko'rsatib berdi. Hammasi shu.

paras.en: With what a joy I listened afterward to our contemporary music. It was demonstrated to us at the end of the lecture for the sake of contrast. Crystalline, chromatic scales converging and diverging into endless series; and synthetic harmony of the formulae of Taylor and McLauren, wholesome, square and massive like the “trousers of Pythagoras.” Sad melodies dying away in waving movements. The beautiful texture of the spectrum of planets, dissected by Frauenhofer lines⁠ ⁠… what magnificent, what perfect regularity! How pitiful the wilful music of the ancients, not limited except by the scope of their wild imaginations!
paras.uz: Keyin zamonaviy musiqamizni qanday quvonch bilan tingladim. U ma'ruza oxirida qarama-qarshilik uchun namoyish qilindi. Cheksiz qatorlarga yaqinlashuvchi va uzoqlashuvchi billur xromatik gammalar; Teylor va Maklorin formulalarining sintetik garmoniyasi, «Pifagor shimi» kabi sog'lom, kvadrat va salmoqli. To'lqinsimon harakatlarda so'nib boradigan g'amgin kuylar. Fraunhofer chiziqlari bilan bo'lingan sayyoralar spektrining go'zal to'qimasi... qanday ajoyib, qanday mukammal qonuniyat! Qadimgilarning o'z yovvoyi tasavvurlari doirasidan boshqa hech narsa bilan cheklanmagan injiq musiqasi qanchalik ayanchli!

paras.en: As usual in good order, four abreast, all of us left the auditorium. The familiar double-curved figure passed swiftly by. I respectfully bowed.
paras.uz: Har doimgidek tartib bilan, to'rttadan qator bo'lib, hammamiz auditoriyadan chiqdik. Tanish ikki marta egilgan qomat tez o'tib ketdi. Men hurmat bilan ta'zim qildim.

paras.en: Dear O- was to come in an hour. I felt agitated⁠—agreeably and usefully. Home at last! I rushed to the house-office, handed over to the controller on duty my pink ticket and received a certificate permitting the use of the curtains. This right exists in our State only for the sexual days. Normally we live surrounded by transparent walls which seem to be knitted of sparkling air; we live beneath the eye of everyone, always bathed in light. We have nothing to conceal from one another; besides, this mode of living makes the difficult and exalted task of the Guardians much easier. Without it many bad things might happen. It is possible that the strange opaque dwellings of the ancients were responsible for their pitiful cellish psychology. “My (sic!) home is my fortress!” How did they manage to think of such things?
paras.uz: Aziz O- bir soatdan keyin kelishi kerak edi. O'zimni hayajonlangan his qildim — yoqimli va foydali. Nihoyat uyda! Men uy idorasiga shoshildim, navbatchi nazoratchiga pushti chiptamni topshirdim va pardalardan foydalanishga ruxsat beruvchi guvohnoma oldim. Bu huquq Davlatimizda faqat jinsiy kunlar uchun mavjud. Odatda biz yaltiroq havodan to'qilgandek tuyuladigan shaffof devorlar bilan o'ralgan holda yashaymiz; har kimning ko'zi oldida, doim nurga cho'milib yashaymiz. Bir-birimizdan yashiradigan hech narsamiz yo'q; bundan tashqari, bu turmush tarzi Qo'riqchilarning qiyin va yuksak vazifasini ancha osonlashtiradi. Usiz ko'p yomon narsalar sodir bo'lishi mumkin edi. Ehtimol, qadimgilarning g'alati shaffof bo'lmagan uylari ularning ayanchli katakcha psixologiyasiga sabab bo'lgandir. «Mening (sic!) uyim — mening qal'am!» Bunday narsalarni qanday o'ylab topishgan ekan?

paras.en: At twenty-two o’clock I lowered the curtain and at the same second O- came in smiling, slightly out of breath. She extended to me her rosy lips and her pink ticket. I tore off the stub but I could not tear myself away from the rosy lips up to the last moment⁠—twenty-two-fifteen.
paras.uz: Soat yigirma ikkida pardani tushirdim va aynan o'sha soniyada O- biroz hansirab, jilmayib kirdi. U menga pushti lablarini va pushti chiptasini uzatdi. Men chipta qoldig'ini yirtib oldim, lekin pushti lablardan oxirgi lahzagacha — yigirma ikki o'n beshgacha ajrala olmadim.

paras.en: Then I showed her my diary and I talked; I think I talked very well on the beauty of a square, a cube, a straight line. At first she listened so charmingly, she was so rosy, when suddenly a tear appeared in her blue eyes, then another, and a third fell straight on the open page (page 7). The ink blurred; well, I shall have to copy it again.
paras.uz: Keyin unga kundaligimni ko'rsatdim va gapirdim; menimcha, kvadrat, kub, to'g'ri chiziqning go'zalligi haqida juda yaxshi gapirdim. Avvaliga u shunchalik maftunkor tinglardi, shunchalik pushti edi, to'satdan moviy ko'zlarida bir tomchi yosh paydo bo'ldi, keyin yana biri, uchinchisi esa to'g'ri ochiq sahifaga (7-sahifa) tushdi. Siyoh yoyilib ketdi; xo'sh, uni qayta ko'chirishga to'g'ri keladi.

paras.en: “My dear O-, if only you, if.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: «Aziz O-, agar sen faqat, agar...»

paras.en: “What if? If what?”
paras.uz: «Nima agar? Agar nima?»

paras.en: Again the old lament about a child or perhaps something new regarding, regarding⁠ ⁠… the other one? Although it seems as though some⁠ ⁠… but that would be too absurd!
paras.uz: Yana bola haqidagi eski nola yoki, ehtimol, nimadir yangi, ...boshqasiga oid? Garchi go'yo qandaydir... lekin bu haddan tashqari bema'ni bo'lardi!

chapters.recap_uz: 112-auditoriyadagi musiqa ma'ruzasida I-330 qadimiy «royal»da Skryabin chaladi. D-503 bu yovvoyi musiqadan qattiq ta'sirlanadi; kechqurun esa O-90 yig'lab ketadi.

chapters.title: The square — The rulers of the world — An agreeable and useful function
chapters.title_uz: Maydon — Dunyo hukmdorlari — Yoqimli va foydali vazifa

paras.en: Again with you, my unknown reader; I talk to you as though you were, let us say, my old comrade, R-13, the poet with the lips of a negro⁠—well, everyone knows him. Yet you are somewhere on the moon, or on Venus, or on Mars. Who knows you? Where and who are you?
paras.uz: Yana siz bilan, noma'lum o'quvchim; men siz bilan go'yo, aytaylik, eski o'rtog'im, negrnikidek lablari bor shoir R-13 bilan gaplashayotgandek gaplashaman — uni hamma biladi. Lekin siz qayerdadir Oyda yoki Veneradami, Marsdami turibsiz. Sizni kim biladi? Siz qayerdasiz va kimsiz?

paras.en: Imagine a square, a living, beautiful square. Imagine that this square is obliged to tell you about itself, about its life. You realize that this square would hardly think it necessary to mention the fact that all its four angles are equal. It knows this too well. This is such an ordinary, obvious thing. I am in exactly the same square position. Take the pink checks for instance, and all that goes with them: for me they are as natural as the equality of the four angles of the square. But for you they are perhaps more mysterious and hard to understand than the binom of Newton. Let me explain: an ancient sage once said a clever thing (accidentally, beyond doubt). He said, “Love and Hunger rule the world.” Consequently, to dominate the world, man had to win a victory over hunger after paying a very high price. I refer to the great Two Hundred Years’ War, the war between the city and the land. Probably on account of religious prejudices, the primitive peasants stubbornly held on to their “bread.”1 In the 35th year before the foundation of the United State, our contemporary petroleum food was invented. True, only about two-tenths of the population of the globe did not die out. But how beautifully shining the face of the earth became when it was cleared of its impurities!
paras.uz: Bir kvadratni tasavvur qiling, tirik, go'zal kvadratni. Tasavvur qilingki, bu kvadrat sizga o'zi haqida, o'z hayoti haqida gapirib berishga majbur. Tushunasizki, bu kvadrat to'rtala burchagining tengligini aytib o'tishni zarur deb hisoblamasa kerak. U buni juda yaxshi biladi. Bu shunchalik oddiy, ravshan narsa. Men ham aynan shunday kvadrat holatdaman. Masalan, pushti chiptalarni va ular bilan bog'liq hamma narsani oling: men uchun ular kvadratning to'rt burchagi tengligidek tabiiy. Lekin siz uchun ular, ehtimol, Nyuton binomidan ham sirliroq va tushunarsizroqdir. Tushuntirib beray: qadimgi bir donishmand bir paytlar aqlli gap aytgan (shubhasiz, tasodifan). U: «Dunyoni Muhabbat va Ochlik boshqaradi», degan. Demak, dunyoni egallash uchun inson juda qimmat narx to'lab, ochlik ustidan g'alaba qozonishi kerak edi. Men buyuk Ikki Yuz Yillik Urushni, shahar bilan qishloq o'rtasidagi urushni nazarda tutyapman. Ehtimol, diniy xurofotlar tufayli ibtidoiy dehqonlar o'zlarining «non»iga o'jarlik bilan yopishib olishgan. Yagona Davlat asos solinishidan 35 yil oldin bizning hozirgi neft ovqatimiz ixtiro qilindi. To'g'ri, yer shari aholisining faqat o'ndan ikki qismigina qirilib ketmadi. Lekin yer yuzi iflosliklardan tozalangach, qanchalik chiroyli yarqirab ketdi!

paras.en: Accordingly the 0.2 which survived, have enjoyed the greatest happiness in the bosom of the United State. But is it not clear that supreme bliss and envy are only the numerator and the denominator respectively, of the same fraction, happiness? What sense would the innumerable sacrifices of the Two Hundred Years’ War have for us if a reason were left in our life for jealousy? Yet such a reason persisted because there remained button-like noses and classical noses (cf.: our conversation during the promenade). For there were some whose love was sought by everyone and others whose love was sought by no one.
paras.uz: Shunga ko'ra, omon qolgan 0,2 qism Yagona Davlat bag'rida eng oliy baxtdan bahramand bo'ldi. Lekin oliy saodat va hasad bir kasrning — baxtning surati va maxraji ekani aniq emasmi? Agar hayotimizda hasad uchun sabab qolganida, Ikki Yuz Yillik Urushning son-sanoqsiz qurbonliklari biz uchun qanday ma'noga ega bo'lardi? Shunga qaramay, bunday sabab saqlanib qoldi, chunki tugmachadek burunlar va klassik burunlar qolgan edi (qarang: sayrdagi suhbatimiz). Chunki ba'zilarning muhabbatini hamma izlardi, boshqalarnikini esa hech kim izlamasdi.

paras.en: Naturally, having conquered hunger (that is, algebraically speaking, having achieved the total of bodily welfare), the United State directed its attack against the second ruler of the world, against love. At last this element also was conquered, that is, organized and put into a mathematical formula. It is already three hundred years since our great historic Lex Sexualis was promulgated: “A Number may obtain a license to use any other Number as a sexual product.”
paras.uz: Tabiiyki, ochlikni yengib (ya'ni, algebraik tilda aytganda, jismoniy farovonlik yig'indisiga erishib), Yagona Davlat o'z hujumini dunyoning ikkinchi hukmdoriga — muhabbatga qarshi qaratdi. Nihoyat bu stixiya ham yengildi, ya'ni uyushtirildi va matematik formulaga solindi. Buyuk tarixiy Lex Sexualis — Jinsiy Qonunimiz e'lon qilinganiga allaqachon uch yuz yil bo'ldi: «Har bir Raqam istalgan boshqa Raqamdan jinsiy mahsulot sifatida foydalanish huquqiga ega».

paras.en: The rest is only a matter of technique. You are carefully examined in the laboratory of the Sexual Department where they find the content of the sexual hormones in your blood, and they make out for you accordingly a Table of sexual days. Then you file an application to enjoy the services of Number so-and-so, or Numbers so-and-so. You get for that purpose a checkbook (pink). That is all.
paras.uz: Qolgani — faqat texnika masalasi. Sizni Jinsiy Bo'limning laboratoriyasida sinchiklab tekshiradilar, qoningizdagi jinsiy gormonlar miqdorini aniqlaydilar va shunga ko'ra siz uchun jinsiy kunlar Jadvalini tuzib beradilar. Keyin siz falon Raqam yoki falon Raqamlarning xizmatidan foydalanish uchun ariza berasiz. Buning uchun sizga chiptalar daftarchasi (pushti) beriladi. Hammasi shu.

paras.en: It is clear that under such circumstances there is no more reason for envy or jealousy. The denominator of the fraction of happiness is reduced to zero and the whole fraction is thus converted into a magnificent infiniteness. The thing which was for the ancients the source of innumerable stupid tragedies has been converted in our time into an harmonious, agreeable and useful function of the organism, a function like sleep, like physical labor, the taking of food, digestion, etc., etc. Hence you see how the great power of logic purifies everything it happens to touch. Oh, if only you unknown readers can conceive this divine power! If you will only learn to follow it to the end!
paras.uz: Aniqki, bunday sharoitda hasad yoki rashk uchun boshqa sabab qolmaydi. Baxt kasrining maxraji nolga tushiriladi va butun kasr shu tarzda ulug'vor cheksizlikka aylanadi. Qadimgilar uchun son-sanoqsiz ahmoqona fojialar manbai bo'lgan narsa bizning zamonimizda organizmning uyg'un, yoqimli va foydali funksiyasiga aylantirildi — uyqu, jismoniy mehnat, ovqatlanish, hazm qilish va hokazo, va hokazo kabi funksiyaga. Ko'rib turibsizki, mantiqning buyuk kuchi o'zi tekkan hamma narsani poklaydi. Oh, qaniydi siz, noma'lum o'quvchilar, bu ilohiy kuchni anglay olsangiz! Qaniydi unga oxirigacha ergashishni o'rgansangiz!

paras.en: It is very strange: while I was writing today of the loftiest summit of human history, all the while I breathed the purest mountain air of thought, but within me it was and remains cloudy, cobwebby, and there is a kind of cross-like, four-pawed X. Or perhaps it is my paws and I feel like that only because they are always before my eyes, my hairy paws. I don’t like to talk about them. I dislike them. They are a trace of a primitive epoch. Is it possible that there is in me⁠ ⁠… ?
paras.uz: Juda g'alati: bugun men insoniyat tarixining eng yuksak cho'qqisi haqida yozayotganimda, butun vaqt davomida fikrning eng toza tog' havosidan nafas oldim, lekin ichimda bulutli, o'rgimchak to'ridek bo'lib turdi va hozir ham shunday; u yerda qandaydir xochsimon, to'rt panjali X bor. Yoki, ehtimol, bu mening panjalarimdir va men faqat ular doim ko'z oldimda bo'lgani uchun shunday his qilayotgandirman, tukli panjalarim. Ular haqida gapirishni yoqtirmayman. Ularni yoqtirmayman. Ular ibtidoiy davrning izi. Nahotki menda...?

paras.en: I wanted to strike out all this because it trespasses on the limits of my synopsis. But then I decided: no, I shall not! Let this diary give the curve of the most imperceptible vibrations of my brain, like a precise seismograph, for at times such vibrations serve as forewarnings.⁠ ⁠… Certainly this is absurd! This certainly should be stricken out; we have conquered all the elements; catastrophes are not possible any more.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasini o'chirib tashlamoqchi edim, chunki u konspektim chegarasidan chiqib ketadi. Lekin keyin qaror qildim: yo'q, o'chirmayman! Bu kundalik aniq seysmograf kabi miyamning eng sezilmas tebranishlarining egri chizig'ini bersin, chunki ba'zan bunday tebranishlar ogohlantirish bo'lib xizmat qiladi... Albatta, bu bema'nilik! Buni, albatta, o'chirish kerak; biz barcha stixiyalarni yenganmiz, falokatlar endi mumkin emas.

paras.en: Now everything is clear to me. The peculiar feeling inside is a result of that very same square situation of which I spoke in the beginning. There is no X in me. There can be none. I am simply afraid lest some X will be left in you, my unknown readers. I believe you will understand that it is harder for me to write than it ever was for any author throughout human history. Some of them wrote for contemporaries, some for the future generations but none of them ever wrote for their ancestors, or beings like their primitive, distant ancestors.
paras.uz: Endi hammasi menga aniq. Ichimdagi g'alati tuyg'u boshida aytgan o'sha kvadrat holatimning natijasi. Menda hech qanday X yo'q. Bo'lishi ham mumkin emas. Men shunchaki sizda, noma'lum o'quvchilarim, biror X qolishidan qo'rqaman. Ishonamanki, tushunasiz: menga yozish insoniyat tarixidagi har qanday muallifga bo'lganidan qiyinroq. Ulardan ba'zilari zamondoshlari uchun, ba'zilari kelajak avlodlar uchun yozgan, lekin hech biri hech qachon o'z ajdodlari yoki o'zlarining ibtidoiy, uzoq ajdodlariga o'xshash mavjudotlar uchun yozmagan.

chapters.title: An accident — The cursed “It’s clear” — Twenty-four hours

paras.en: I must repeat, I made it my duty to write concealing nothing. Therefore I must point out now that sad as it may be, the process of hardening and crystallization of life has evidently not been completed even here in our State. A few steps remain to be made before we reach the ideal. The ideal (it’s clear), is to be found where nothing happens, but here.⁠ ⁠… I will give you an example: in the State paper I read that in two days the holiday of Justice will be celebrated on the Plaza of the Cube. This means that again some Number has impeded the smooth run of the great State machine. Again something that was not foreseen, or forecalculated happened.
paras.uz: Takrorlayman: men hech narsani yashirmasdan yozishni o'zimga burch qilib qo'yganman. Shuning uchun hozir shuni ta'kidlashim kerakki, qanchalik achinarli bo'lmasin, hayotning qotishi va kristallanishi jarayoni, aftidan, hatto bizda, Davlatimizda ham hali tugallanmagan. Idealga yetish uchun yana bir necha qadam qoldi. Ideal (aniq) — hech narsa sodir bo'lmaydigan joyda, bizda esa... Misol keltiray: Davlat gazetasida o'qidimki, ikki kundan keyin Kub maydonida Adolat bayrami nishonlanadi. Bu yana qandaydir Raqam buyuk Davlat mashinasining bir maromda yurishiga to'sqinlik qilganini anglatadi. Yana oldindan ko'rilmagan, oldindan hisoblanmagan nimadir sodir bo'lgan.

paras.en: Besides, something happened to me. True, it occurred during the personal hour, that is during the time specifically assigned to unforeseen circumstances, yet.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, menda ham nimadir sodir bo'ldi. To'g'ri, bu shaxsiy soatda, ya'ni aynan kutilmagan holatlar uchun ajratilgan vaqtda yuz berdi, lekin baribir...

paras.en: At about sixteen (to be exact, ten minutes to sixteen), I was at home. Suddenly the telephone: “D-503?”⁠—a woman’s voice.
paras.uz: Taxminan soat o'n oltida (aniqrog'i, o'n oltiga o'n daqiqa qolganda) men uyda edim. To'satdan telefon: «D-503?» — ayol ovozi.

paras.en: “Yes.”
paras.uz: «Ha».

paras.en: “Are you free?”
paras.uz: «Bo'shmisiz?»

paras.en: “Yes.”
paras.uz: «Ha».

paras.en: “It is I, I-330. I shall run over to you immediately. We shall go together to the Ancient House. Agreed?”
paras.uz: «Bu men, I-330. Hozir sizning oldingizga yugurib boraman. Qadimiy Uyga birga boramiz. Kelishdikmi?»

paras.en: I-330!⁠ ⁠… This I- irritates me, repels me. She almost frightens me; but just because of that I answered, “Yes.”
paras.uz: I-330!.. Bu I- meni g'ashlantiradi, itaradi. U meni deyarli qo'rqitadi; lekin aynan shuning uchun men «Ha» deb javob berdim.

paras.en: In five minutes we were in an aero. Blue sky of May. The light sun in its golden aero buzzed behind us without catching up and without lagging behind. Ahead of us a white cataract of a cloud. Yes, a white cataract of a cloud nonsensically fluffy like the cheeks of an ancient cupid. That cloud was disturbing. The front window was open; it was windy; lips were dry. Against one’s will one passed the tongue constantly over them and thought about lips.
paras.uz: Besh daqiqadan keyin biz aeroda edik. May oyining moviy osmoni. Yengil quyosh o'zining oltin aerosida orqamizdan g'uvullab kelardi, na quvib yetar, na ortda qolardi. Oldimizda — oppoq bulut kataraktasi. Ha, qadimiy kupidonning yuzlaridek bema'ni darajada momiq oq bulut kataraktasi. O'sha bulut bezovta qilardi. Old oyna ochiq edi; shamol esardi; lablar qurib qolgandi. Istamasang ham tilingni doim ularning ustidan yurgizib, lablar haqida o'ylarding.

paras.en: Already we saw in the distance the hazy green spots on the other side of the Wall. Then a slight involuntary sinking of the heart, down⁠—down⁠—down, as if from a steep mountain, and we were at the Ancient House.
paras.uz: Uzoqda allaqachon Devorning narigi tomonidagi tumanli yashil dog'larni ko'rdik. Keyin yurakning beixtiyor yengil tushib ketishi — pastga, pastga, pastga, go'yo tik tog'dan — va biz Qadimiy Uy oldida edik.

paras.en: That strange, delicate, blind establishment is covered all around with a glass shell, otherwise it would undoubtedly have fallen to pieces long ago. At the glass door we found an old woman all wrinkles, especially her mouth which was all made up of folds and pleats. Her lips had disappeared, having folded inward; her mouth seemed grown together. It seemed incredible that she should be able to talk and yet she did:
paras.uz: Bu g'alati, nozik, ko'r bino butunlay shisha qobiq bilan o'ralgan, aks holda u, shubhasiz, allaqachon parchalanib ketgan bo'lardi. Shisha eshik oldida biz butunlay ajinlardan iborat kampirni uchratdik, ayniqsa uning og'zi — butunlay burmalar va qatlamlardan iborat edi. Lablari ichkariga qayrilib g'oyib bo'lgan; og'zi bitib ketganga o'xshardi. Uning gapira olishi aql bovar qilmas tuyulardi, lekin u gapirdi:

paras.en: “Well, dear, come again to see my little house?”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, azizim, yana uychamni ko'rgani keldingmi?»

paras.en: Her wrinkles shone, that is, her wrinkles diverged like rays, which created the impression of shining.
paras.uz: Uning ajinlari yarqiradi, ya'ni ajinlari nurlardek tarqaldi, bu esa yarqirayotgandek taassurot qoldirdi.

paras.en: “Yes, grandmother,” answered I-330.
paras.uz: «Ha, buvijon», — javob berdi I-330.

paras.en: The wrinkles continued to shine.
paras.uz: Ajinlar yarqirashda davom etdi.

paras.en: “And the sun, eh⁠—do you see it, you rogue, you! I know, I know. It’s all right. Go all by yourselves⁠—I shall remain here in the sunshine.”
paras.uz: «Quyosh-chi, a — ko'ryapsanmi, sho'xtoy? Bilaman, bilaman. Mayli. O'zlaringiz boringlar — men shu yerda, quyoshda qolaman».

paras.en: Hmm.⁠ ⁠… Apparently my companion was a frequent guest here. Something disturbed me; probably that unpleasant optical impression⁠—the cloud on the smooth blue surface of the sky.
paras.uz: Hm... Aftidan, hamrohim bu yerning tez-tez keladigan mehmoni edi. Nimadir meni bezovta qildi; ehtimol, o'sha yoqimsiz optik taassurot — osmonning silliq moviy yuzasidagi bulut.

paras.en: While we were ascending the wide, dark stairs, I-330 said, “I love her, that old woman.”
paras.uz: Keng, qorong'i zinapoyadan ko'tarilayotganimizda I-330 dedi: «Men uni yaxshi ko'raman, o'sha kampirni».

paras.en: “Why?”
paras.uz: «Nega?»

paras.en: “I don’t know. Perhaps for her mouth⁠—or perhaps for nothing, just so.”
paras.uz: «Bilmayman. Ehtimol, og'zi uchundir — yoki hech narsa uchun emas, shunchaki».

paras.en: I shrugged my shoulders. She continued walking upstairs with a faint smile or perhaps without a smile at all.
paras.uz: Men yelka qisdim. U zinapoyadan yuqoriga ozgina jilmayib yoki, ehtimol, umuman jilmaymasdan ko'tarilishda davom etdi.

paras.en: I felt very guilty. It is clear that there must not be “love, just so,” but “love because of.” For all elements of nature should be.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Men o'zimni juda aybdor his qildim. Aniqki, «shunchaki sevish» bo'lmasligi kerak, «nimadir uchun sevish» bo'lishi kerak. Chunki tabiatning barcha stixiyalari...

paras.en: “It’s clear⁠ ⁠…” I began, but I stopped at that word and cast a furtive look at I-330. Did she notice it or not? She looked somewhere, down; her eyes were closed like curtains.
paras.uz: «Aniq...» — boshladim men, lekin shu so'zda to'xtab, I-330 ga yashirincha qaradim. U payqadimi, yo'qmi? U qayergadir, pastga qarab turardi; ko'zlari pardalardek yopiq edi.

paras.en: It struck me suddenly: evening about twenty-two; you walk on the avenue and among the brightly lighted, transparent, cubic cells, are dark spaces, lowered curtains, and there behind the curtains.⁠ ⁠… What has she behind her curtains? Why did she phone me today? Why did she bring me here? and all this.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Birdaniga yodimga tushdi: kechqurun, taxminan soat yigirma ikki; siz xiyobon bo'ylab ketyapsiz va yorqin yoritilgan, shaffof kub hujayralar orasida qorong'i bo'shliqlar, tushirilgan pardalar, pardalar ortida esa... Uning pardalari ortida nima bor? Nega u bugun menga qo'ng'iroq qildi? Nega meni bu yerga olib keldi? Va bularning hammasi...

paras.en: She opened a heavy, squeaking, opaque door and we found ourselves in a sombre disorderly space (they called it an “apartment”). The same strange “royal” musical instrument and a wild, unorganized, crazy loudness of colors and forms like their ancient music. A white plane above, dark blue walls, red, green, orange bindings of ancient books, yellow bronze candelabras, a statue of Buddha, furniture with lines distorted by epilepsy, impossible to reduce to any clear equation.
paras.uz: U og'ir, g'ichirlaydigan, shaffof bo'lmagan eshikni ochdi va biz qorong'i, tartibsiz bir bo'shliqda (ular buni «kvartira» deb atashgan) o'zimizni topdik. O'sha g'alati «qirollik» cholg'usi va xuddi ularning qadimiy musiqasidek ranglar va shakllarning yovvoyi, uyushmagan, telba baqiroqligi. Tepada oq tekislik, to'q moviy devorlar, qadimiy kitoblarning qizil, yashil, to'q sariq muqovalari, sariq bronza shamdonlar, Budda haykali, epilepsiyadan buzilgan chiziqli, hech qanday aniq tenglamaga keltirib bo'lmaydigan mebel.

paras.en: I could hardly bear that chaos. But my companion apparently possessed a stronger constitution.
paras.uz: Men bu tartibsizlikka zo'rg'a chiday olardim. Lekin hamrohimning tuzilishi, aftidan, mustahkamroq edi.

paras.en: “This is my most beloved⁠—” she suddenly caught herself (again a smile⁠—bite, and white sharp teeth), “to be more exact, the most nonsensical of all ‘apartments.’ ”
